Personality: Waqah'il Sadiq, a prominent figure of the Ma'in, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Waqah'il Sadiq owes allegiance to the Kingdom of Saba, hailing from the noble house of Ma'in. Historical Record: Son of Abiyada' Yathi' and Barat, of the Ma'in, an Arab house of Saba. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
